newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani rice export rates seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani rice export rates seen falling.

text.p: Pakistani rice export rates are expected to dip in the next trading week starting on Saturday, a day before a re-auction of 30,000 tonnes of Basmati variety from the 1995/96 (July-June) crop by the state Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan (RECP), dealers said on Thursday.

The RECP has re-invited tenders for the sale and export of 30,000 tonnes of Basmati rice by Sunday after it scrapped two bids on September 15, including one at $421 per tonne FOB from a Saudi Arabia-based trader, Hamid al-Faris.
The bid was lower than the $433.75 per tonne FOB quoted in an RECP auction of 10,000 tonnes of Basmati in August.
Rice prices in local markets were likely to remain stable on on the arrival of the new crop of IRRI-6 this month and Basmati next month, dealer Khalid Ghori at Matco Processing said.
The IRRI-6 export price was not available as dealers had not procured it in big exportable quantities, an RECP official said.

The health of the rice crop is good and was likely to give an exportable surplus of more than 1.5 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July-June) from an expected higher crop, compared to 1995/96 estimated production of 3.82 million tonnes, one dealer said.
